findings.title: parseBody() after c.req.formData() now breaks; no test covers ordering
findings.why_it_matters: On the base commit, `parseFormData` called `request.formData()`, which for a HonoRequest is served straight from `bodyCache.formData` when `c.req.formData()` had already run. The reviewed code instead calls `request.arrayBuffer()`; with only `formData` cached, `HonoRequest.#cachedBody('arrayBuffer')` re-serialises the cached FormData via `new Response(formData).arrayBuffer()`, which emits a fresh multipart body with a NEW random boundary, and `bufferToFormData` then parses those bytes with the ORIGINAL request Content-Type. Reproduced with a scratch script against the reviewed tree: multipart -> parseBody rejects with `Failed to parse body as FormData.`; urlencoded -> parseBody returns a garbage single key containing the multipart envelope, and because line 130 overwrites `bodyCache.formData` with that bad promise, a subsequent `c.req.formData().get('message')` returns `null`. The same script against base body.ts returns `{message:'hello'}` and keeps the cache intact in all three calls. The full suite (body/buffer/validator/request tests) is green, so nothing in the diff or the existing tests exercises the `formData()` -> `parseBody()` order that `validator('form')` already guards for (validator.ts:115 checks `bodyCache.formData` first). Mirroring that guard restores the old behaviour and keeps the case-insensitive path for the uncached case.
evidence: src/utils/body.ts:126 `const arrayBuffer = await (request as Request).arrayBuffer()` (base called `(request as Request).formData()`, which `#cachedBody('formData')` served from the cache)
src/utils/body.ts:130 `request.bodyCache.formData = formDataPromise as unknown as FormData` overwrites the previously good cached FormData with the mis-parsed one

src/request.ts:228-235 `const anyCachedKey = Object.keys(bodyCache)[0]` ... `return new Response(body)[key]()` -- when only `formData` is cached, `arrayBuffer()` re-encodes the FormData with a new boundary
src/validator/validator.ts:115 `if (c.req.bodyCache.formData) { formData = await c.req.bodyCache.formData }` -- the validator already guards this ordering; parseBody does not

Scratch repro (tmp/repro-formdata-then-parsebody.ts, bundled with esbuild, run with node) on reviewed tree: `multipart THREW: Failed to parse body as FormData.`; `urlencoded parseBody() after formData() -> {"------formdata-undici-055236489350
Content-Disposition: form-data; name":""message"

hello
------formdata-undici-055236489350--
"}`; `urlencoded formData() again -> null`

Same script against base body.ts (git show 97287029:src/utils/body.ts): `multipart parseBody() after formData() -> {"message":"hello"}`, `urlencoded parseBody() after formData() -> {"message":"hello"}`, `formData() again -> hello`

`vitest --run --project main src/utils/body.test.ts src/utils/buffer.test.ts src/validator/validator.test.ts src/request.test.ts` -> 144 passed, 1 skipped: no existing test calls `formData()` before `parseBody()` on a HonoRequest

residual_risks: src/middleware/method-override/index.ts:74,92 still matches Content-Type with case-sensitive `startsWith('multipart/form-data')` / `startsWith('application/x-www-form-urlencoded')`, so a `Multipart/Form-Data` request that now parses in parseBody/validator will still not be method-overridden. Out of this diff's files, but the same bug class as #5060.
testing_gaps: The new cache write at src/utils/body.ts:130 is justified by the comment 'Cache so that a later c.req.formData() reuses the already-consumed body', but no test asserts the value: src/request.test.ts:377-381 only does `expect(async () => await req.text()).not.toThrow()` style checks after `parseBody()`. A scratch run shows `parseBody()` -> `formData().get('message')` -> `'hello'` works; add that assertion (and `text()` returning the original multipart body) to `describe('req.parseBody()')` so the caching contract is actually pinned.

The HonoRequest branch of `parseFormData` (`request instanceof HonoRequest` -> `request.raw.headers` + `bodyCache.formData` write) with a mixed-case Content-Type is only exercised through plain `Request` objects in src/utils/body.test.ts; an end-to-end `app.post('/', c => c.json(await c.req.parseBody()))` request with `Multipart/Form-Data; boundary=...` would cover the branch the issue actually reported.
